title: Design Custom Baseball Jerseys (2026)
verdict: To design custom baseball jerseys in 2026, start in Wooter's builder. Choose a baseball style, set the colors and trim, add your script or logo, and the preview and price update with each change. Wooter's designers will also draw the jersey for free.

Boombah's builder is the alternative to try for sublimated jerseys and pants. Champro's Uniform Builder suits teams with a dealer. Custom Ink's Design Lab is for printed jerseys. Nike Team designs with its dealers.
steps_title: How to design a baseball jersey

steps.name: Choose the cut
steps.text: Full button, two button or pullover. This sets the look more than any color.

steps.name: Set body and sleeves
steps.text: One color, or a contrasting sleeve for a raglan look.

steps.name: Add trim
steps.text: Piping down the placket and around the sleeves, or pinstripes. Pick one.

steps.name: Letter the chest
steps.text: Team name or city in script or block, angled or straight.

steps.name: Number it
steps.text: Large on the back, small on the front. Make sure both stand out from the body color.

steps.name: Enter the roster and approve
steps.text: Names, numbers and sizes per player, then check the proof.

ranking.fit: Coaches and team parents who want to design the jersey themselves, with a designer in reserve.
ranking.lacks: Design takes minutes. The jerseys take three to four weeks after approval.

ranking.fit: Baseball teams that want sublimated jerseys and pants from one maker's own factories.
ranking.lacks: Its baseball pages quote different lead times. Get the date in writing.

ranking.fit: Teams with a local dealer that want a cut-and-sew Juice jersey or a lower-cost Splash one.
ranking.lacks: The builder saves a design. A dealer account places the order.

ranking.fit: Rec and company teams that need a printed button-front jersey in about two weeks.
ranking.lacks: Stock garments with your print added, not a jersey built from your pattern.

ranking.fit: School programs that want Nike and plan a season ahead with a dealer.
ranking.lacks: Build-to-order takes 30, 60 or 90 days. Personalized stock arrives within three weeks.

why: A baseball jersey is designed in layers. The cut first, then the body color, then the trim, then the script and numbers on top.
Wooter's builder follows that order and starts from finished styles, so you are adjusting a jersey that already works. Pinstripes, piping and sleeve trim are style choices, not extra steps.
If the script is the sticking point, send the team name to the designers. Lettering is the part they are best at.

criteria.name: Cut options
criteria.text: Full button, two button and pullover.

criteria.name: Lettering
criteria.text: A chest script that looks drawn, not typed.

criteria.name: Matching pants
criteria.text: The design carried below the belt.

criteria.name: Proof
criteria.text: A mockup to approve before production.

faq.q: Full button, two button or pullover?
faq.a: Full button is the classic. Two button and pullover are lighter and popular in travel ball.
Yes. Pinstripe is among the styles in Wooter's catalog.

faq.q: Where does the front number go?
faq.a: Lower left chest, under the script, is the usual spot.

faq.q: Do I need a vector logo?
faq.a: It gives the cleanest result. A sharp PNG is enough to start, and the designers can rebuild it.
Yes at Wooter. You pay when you order.
